Job Description Summary
As part of the GE Aerospace Digital Technology organization supporting the Defense & Systems (D&S) business, the Director, Program Management owns delivery across the Defense and Systems Customer Experience (DSCX) portfolio. This is a people-leadership role accountable for on-time delivery, program operating rhythms, dependency and risk management, and the scope, schedule, and cost tradeoffs for every program. This person will lead a team of program and project managers, set the delivery standard, and own the $25+MM CX budget in partnership with Finance and Business Operations. This person will be the single point of accountability for predictable execution and for escalating early when a dependency or decision threatens delivery. Job Description
Why This Role Exists
DSCX owns 30+ digital products for Defense & Systems. Today our technical product managers wear three hats for their products: product management, project management, and operations. We are dividing that load across three dedicated functions, and this role will build out the program management discipline, starting with on-time delivery across the portfolio. This role is planned to have 4-6 direct reports, program and project managers, and owns the $25+MM CX budget with Finance and Business Operations. Your charge is to build standard operating rhythms and artifacts, and then coach and train your team to hold them. You should be experienced with AI and know where it creates opportunity to expand what the team can deliver.

Environment
The DSCX portfolio runs primarily on AWS, Palantir Foundry, or through SaaS based 3rd party solutions, with on-premise implementations supported for customers whose data sensitivity requires it. Delivery runs through Rally and Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow is our system of record for incidents, change, and defect management. The portfolio carries a $25+MM annual budget across the product lines.

Roles and Responsibilities

Delivery

• Own on-time delivery (OTD) across the DSCX portfolio. OTD is the primary measure of this role. You set the target, run the cadence that surfaces risk against it, and close the gap.

• Run the operating rhythm so problems surface early. The weekly and monthly operating reviews (WOR and MOR), standups, reviews, and retros exist to make a slipping date visible weeks out, not on the date.

• Run Daily Visual Management across the portfolio. Delivery status and blockers are visible daily, which is what makes early escalation possible rather than aspirational.

• Make status honest and comparable. Every major program reports RAG status, milestones, and a path to green against one standard, so leadership compares programs instead of interpreting formats.

Dependency and Risk

• Keep programs from stalling on each other. You hold the dependency picture across DSCX and the partner teams we depend on, including Palantir, and resolve conflicts before they become schedule impacts.

• Drive risks to closure with a named owner and a date. The RAID log is the mechanism. Closure inside the committed date is the measure.

• Escalate early and with a recommendation. When a decision or dependency threatens a committed date, the sponsor hears it from you while there is still time to act, with the tradeoff already framed.

Scope, Schedule, and Cost

• Own the tradeoffs. Every program has a scope, schedule, and cost triangle. You either make the call or frame the decision for whoever should.

• Own the $25+MM CX budget with Finance and Business Operations, reconciled monthly, with committed versus actual accurate enough to plan against.

• Control change. Approved scope, schedule, and budget changes are documented and traceable, so a program's history explains its current state.

GDIT is seeking a Senior DevOps Engineer (AWS / Windows) to join our National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) team in Rockville, MD. You will use Terraform to create, modify, and automate the AWS infrastructure that hosts NIAID's Windows-based scientific and business applications.

Our ideal candidate is a senior engineer who manages infrastructure through code. You have built and maintained AWS environments in Terraform, delivered changes through Git-based pipelines, and automated the manual work that usually comes with hosting Windows applications. You are as comfortable writing a Terraform module as you are troubleshooting an application running on IIS.
As a senior member of our Cloud DevOps team, you will run and improve our existing AWS platform and help move the remaining on-prem Windows workloads into AWS. You will work closely with application owners, software developers, and security teams, own your work from design through operations, and help shape how the team builds and ships infrastructure. After-hours work is occasionally required for planned maintenance or for troubleshooting service-impacting outages.

HOW A SENIOR DEVOPS ENGINEER WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

• Create, modify, and maintain AWS infrastructure and services in Terraform. That means writing new modules and configurations, extending existing ones, and managing state across environments.

• Deliver infrastructure changes through GitHub Actions and AWS CodeBuild pipelines, so every change is reviewed in a pull request, planned, and applied the same way every time.

• Build and maintain the AWS environment that hosts Windows Server and IIS applications running .NET, including EC2, load balancers, AWS WAF, Route 53, IAM, and TLS certificates, all defined in Terraform.

• Migrate on-prem Windows applications into AWS and improve them once they land, including moving applications into containers on Amazon ECS where it makes sense.

• Automate routine operational work such as certificate renewal, service account credential rotation, patching, and service restarts, using Terraform, PowerShell, and AWS Systems Manager. Where possible, turn these tasks into self-service options for application owners.

• Troubleshoot problems across the application and infrastructure layers (IIS, .NET, networking, and AWS services) and fix the root cause in code rather than by hand.

• Build and tune monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch and native AWS observability services, including metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards, and the CloudWatch agent on Windows servers, all defined in Terraform. Set service level objectives and alerts so the team hears about real problems before users do.

• Work with the security team to remediate vulnerabilities and apply hardening standards to Windows servers and AWS resources.

• Review teammates' Terraform and pipeline changes, share what works, and help shape the team's standards for infrastructure as code and deployments.

Required Experience:

• BA/BS and 7+ years of related IT experience, or equivalent experience. This must include 3+ years of hands-on DevOps or cloud engineering in AWS supporting production workloads.

• 3+ years using Terraform to create, modify, and automate AWS infrastructure, including writing modules, safely changing existing configurations, and managing remote state.

• Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines that deploy infrastructure changes, using GitHub Actions, AWS CodeBuild, or similar tools

You'll operate autonomously in a fully remote role, collaborating with a talented, globally distributed team to design and implement the protocol, signer software, and tooling that move Bitcoin in and out of the Stacks blockchain. This is a hands-on engineering role with real ownership over some of the most critical, security-sensitive infrastructure in the Stacks ecosystem.

Outcomes You'll Drive

•
A secure, correct peg between Bitcoin and Stacks
Deposits and withdrawals move real Bitcoin reliably and safely, backed by threshold-signing coordination that holds up under adversarial and edge-case conditions, not just the happy path.

•
Signer software that performs under real-world conditions
The sBTC signer network stays healthy, observable, and resilient in the presence of faults, network partitions, and delays - because it's securing real Bitcoin, not test funds.

•
Tooling that makes sBTC easier to build on, monitor, and debug
CLI clients, monitoring utilities, and benchmarking tools give internal teams and external partners clear visibility into signer health and peg operations, reducing the time it takes to diagnose and resolve issues.

•
A codebase built for scale and change
Strong engineering fundamentals - scalable architecture, disciplined refactoring, thorough testing - mean the sBTC protocol can absorb new features and integrations without accumulating risk.

What You'll Do

Core sBTC Protocol Engineering

• Contribute to developing, maintaining, and testing the sBTC protocol and its signer software.

• Design and implement core peg mechanics - deposits and withdrawals - and the threshold-signing coordination that secures the sBTC wallet.

• Implement rigorous and thorough monitoring and testing to meet the stringent security and performance requirements of a system safeguarding real Bitcoin.

• Design and implement supporting tools and utilities, such as CLI clients, applications that support moving sBTC on or off the Stacks blockchain, and utilities for monitoring signer health, benchmarking, or debugging.

• Collaborate with other teams on new product features across the Stacks blockchain, including applications that support moving sBTC on or off the Stacks blockchain and protocol integrations.

• Work closely with internal teams and external partners, communicating design decisions and trade-offs clearly as sBTC integrates with new products and partner systems.

What We're Looking For

•
5+ years of experience building and shipping products.

Strong, demonstrated engineering fundamentals , including scalability, architecture, refactoring, algorithms, and testing.

• Experience building and operating security- or reliability-critical backend systems.

•
Strong written and verbal communication skills , with the ability to work effectively with both internal teams and external partners.

Nice to Have

• Expertise in Rust, which is the primary language of the sBTC codebase.

• Working knowledge of blockchains, distributed systems, peer-to-peer systems, and decentralization.

• Familiarity with the Bitcoin protocol.

• Knowledge of multi-party cryptography.

• Experience testing distributed systems for behaviors in the presence of faults, network partitions, and network delays.

title: Data Analyst - Platform Migration
description:
We're hiring a Business & Data Analyst to support the consolidation of acquired screening and adjacent HR tech businesses into Veremark . You'll work under the direction of our M&A PMO, delivering analysis and data tasks against our established integration playbook.
Veremark is a background screening and workforce trust technology company. Employers use us to run pre-employment checks, to verify criminal records, right to work, references, identity, credit and more, through our platform and integrate us with their ATS and HR systems.
You'll sit in the PMO's lean core team, taking direction from the Program Director and supporting the operations, HR and finance leads, product and engineering. Your job is the data: understanding what each acquired platform holds, getting it into Veremark correctly, and showing it's right. You'll also make each integration quicker than the last, by building reusable mappings, queries and checks.
What you'll do
Profile and map

• Profile each acquired platform's data with SQL: volumes, client usage, active vs dormant accounts, data quality and the edge cases the documentation misses.

• Build and maintain field-level mappings between the two data models, covering check types, client configurations, candidate records and history.

• Raise gaps between what the source holds and what Veremark needs, with evidence, so the product team can decide.

Migrate and prove

• Validate and reconcile each client cohort before and after migration: counts, key values, statuses and outcomes.

• Log every difference and trace it to a cause: the source data, the mapping or the expectation.

• Prepare the evidence pack that lets a cohort be signed off, and support UAT with the people who check it.

Integrations and commercial data

• Keep an inventory of each client's ATS/HRIS integrations, API consumers and webhooks, and their migration status.

• Map products, price books and contract terms, and help Finance reconcile billing between each acquired platform and Veremark .

Report

• Own the migration dashboards for every integration in progress and contribute to the Programme Director's weekly update.

• Give Customer Success and Sales the client data they need to plan each move.

• Use AI to work faster: query data with prompts, draft and review SQL, generate first-pass mappings and documentation, and automate routine checks, always verifying results against the source.

Make each integration faster

• Build a reusable library of profiling and reconciliation SQL, mapping templates and sign-off checklists.

• Feed what you learn back into the integration playbook after each deal.

• Where needed, review a target company's data before a deal closes, so we know what we're taking on.

Must have

•

• 3+ years as a data analyst , with hands-on work on at least one data migration, platform consolidation or system implementation. Tell us what you moved, how much, and what went wrong.

• Strong SQL: joins, CTEs, window functions and aggregation, used to profile unfamiliar data and reconcile a source against a target.

• Confident with AI and new tools: you already use AI in your daily work, for example querying data with prompts, drafting and reviewing SQL with an LLM, or using AI features in your BI tool. You know where it saves time, and you check what it produces against the data.

• Data mapping and validation: you've written field-level mappings, tested migrated data against them and investigated the differences.
